abstract_summary: Multi-round reflection lets agents built on large language models recover from failures within a single task, but each task remains an isolated episode: lessons learned across many reflection rounds on one task are discarded before the next begins. We study this gap on a code-generation task: from a scientific paper...

concerns: The headline human evaluation has collapsed inter-rater reliability: Fleiss' kappa = -0.01 for binary usability and Likert ICCs between -0.09 and 0.33, all below common reliability thresholds, so the reported Pass@1 and quality gains are not established by a reliable independent measurement.
Raw rater-level records were deleted after 14 days, preventing reconstruction of condition-specific denominators, paired uncertainty intervals, or audit of the headline point estimates.

The internal VLM reward signal shows weak or negative agreement with human ratings (Pearson r = -0.17, Spearman rho = -0.20, Cohen's kappa = -0.07), so the memory-write and revision signal is not calibrated against the independent outcome it is claimed to improve.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: Although the method is clearly described and thoughtfully architected to isolate memory growth from prompt formatting and task ordering, the headline empirical validation relies on a human study whose inter-rater reliability entirely collapsed (Fleiss' kappa = -0.01, ICCs near zero or negative). Because the independent corroboration lacks statistical reliability and raw data cannot be audited, scientific uncertainty precludes promotion.

of different sizes. Each snapshot is evaluated on the same disjoint probe tasks in read-only mode, so
probe outputs cannot be written back to memory and task order cannot explain differences between
conditions (§4.3). Because the same VLM both scores rendered keyframes and gates memory writes,
using VLM scores as the headline metric would risk evaluator leakage (the reward model is also
the judge, so the system could appear to improve simply by drifting toward the preferences of the
VLM). We therefore use blind human judgement of first-attempt videos together with reflection
rounds as the headline evidence, and report VLM scores only as auxiliary diagnostics (§4.5).
This work makes three contributions.
• We proposeManimAgent, a self-evolving multi-agent system that narrows the inter-task gap
with a VLM reward source and a dual-channel EMB, with no weight updates (§3).

blocking_reasons: The headline human evaluation has collapsed inter-rater reliability: Fleiss' kappa = -0.01 for binary usability and Likert ICCs between -0.09 and 0.33, all below common reliability thresholds, so the reported Pass@1 and quality gains are not established by a reliable independent measurement.
Raw rater-level records were deleted after 14 days, preventing reconstruction of condition-specific denominators, paired uncertainty intervals, or audit of the headline point estimates.

The internal VLM reward signal shows weak or negative agreement with human ratings (Pearson r = -0.17, Spearman rho = -0.20, Cohen's kappa = -0.07), so the memory-write and revision signal is not calibrated against the independent outcome it is claimed to improve.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline outcome is measured by blind human raters separate from the VLM reward model, but the human measurement itself has near-zero or negative inter-rater reliability.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Blind human raters provide binary usability decisions and five Likert dimensions on first-attempt videos.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: A VLM reviewer scores rendered keyframes on logical flow, layout/occlusion, and accuracy to drive visual revisions and gate positive and negative memory writes.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: While point estimates show monotonic improvements from EMB@0 to EMB@200, the complete absence of inter-rater agreement among human evaluators and the lack of confidence intervals leave the primary empirical gains uncorroborated by reliable measurement.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The authors perform a frozen-probe snapshot evaluation tracking Human Pass@1, reflection rounds, and Likert quality ratings across memory sizes and baselines. However, the reported human evaluation exhibits near-zero or negative inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' kappa = -0.01; Likert ICCs between -0.09 and 0.33 across 54 raters), and the raw ratings were deleted, preventing verification or uncertainty estimation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using 54 blind human raters on fixed-probe tasks, completely separate from the internal VLM reviewer score.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Blind human rater evaluations measuring Human Pass@1 and a 5-dimension Likert Human Quality score on first-attempt videos.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: A multimodal VLM reviewer scores rendered keyframes across pedagogical axes to drive multi-round code revisions and gate positive/negative memory consolidation.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report that VLM-human correlation is weak or negative (Pearson r = -0.17) and that human inter-rater reliability is below acceptable thresholds, alongside evaluating only on Manim across limited domains.
primary.method_assessment: The system decomposes tasks into scenes, uses a Coder agent guided by retrieved positive reference examples and negative failure pitfalls, executes Manim renders in a sandbox, and relies on an internal VLM reviewer to guide revisions and gate memory consolidation.
primary.quality_rationale: Although the method is clearly described and thoughtfully architected to isolate memory growth from prompt formatting and task ordering, the headline empirical validation relies on a human study whose inter-rater reliability entirely collapsed (Fleiss' kappa = -0.01, ICCs near zero or negative). Because the independent corroboration lacks statistical reliability and raw data cannot be audited, scientific uncertainty precludes promotion.
primary.scoped_contribution: ManimAgent introduces a self-evolving multi-agent framework that transfers visual programming experience across animation tasks via a dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank without parameter updates.

scholarly_quality.rationale: Although the method is clearly described and thoughtfully architected to isolate memory growth from prompt formatting and task ordering, the headline empirical validation relies on a human study whose inter-rater reliability entirely collapsed (Fleiss' kappa = -0.01, ICCs near zero or negative). Because the independent corroboration lacks statistical reliability and raw data cannot be audited, scientific uncertainty precludes promotion.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report that VLM-human correlation is weak or negative (Pearson r = -0.17) and that human inter-rater reliability is below acceptable thresholds, alongside evaluating only on Manim across limited domains.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
